EXPLAINED: CHINA’S ARUNACHAL POWER PLAY

Fresh face-offs along the India-China border have brought Arunachal Pradesh into focus, raising concerns over Beijing’s intentions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

On October 22, ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur confirmed confrontations at multiple locations along the Arunachal border, with tensions centred around Asaphila in Upper Subansiri district.

Is China pursuing a strategy of salami slicing—gradually testing Indian positions and pushing boundaries without triggering a full-scale conflict?

With China enjoying an infrastructure advantage in Tibet, India is accelerating border connectivity and surveillance to strengthen its defences.

Are these isolated confrontations or part of a calculated strategy to keep India under pressure?

Read more about Beijing’s Arunachal gambit in the latest issue of India Today Magazine.

results.title: Decoding the LAC: Why Headline Sensationalism Misses the Ground Reality of India-China Border Dynamics?
results.description:
Decoding the LAC: Why Headline Sensationalism Misses the Ground Reality of India-China Border Dynamics? Already viewed by > 450,000

Media headlines thrive on sensationalism and panic, but national security is governed by cold terrain friction, historical legalities, and strategic calculus and military prowess.

In a recent deep-dive discussion on Ankit Inspires India I, alongside my fellow veteran Maj Gen Sanjay Meston, dismantled prevailing ambiguities and viral social media narratives surrounding India’s northern borders—revealing what routine media reporting misses by anchoring our analysis strictly in professional military experience and verifiable open-source research.

Key Insights from the Discussion

1. Deconstructing "Face-Offs" vs. Incursions: The Line of Actual Control is not a mutually demarcated international border; it is an alignment marked by differing perceptions and overlapping patrol limits. Stand-offs occur when simultaneous patrols encounter each other along disputed pockets—managed strictly through structured protocols and Confidence Building Measures (CBMs), not spontaneous tactical collapse.

2. The Arunachal Reality & Historical Context: From the legal framework of the 1914 Simla Convention and the McMahon Line to the 1962 conflict dynamics and Major Bob Khathing’s consolidation of Tawang, Indian sovereignty over Arunachal Pradesh is unassailable. Viral maps and satellite imagery often mistake border village infrastructure on China’s side for incursions, missing the substantial multi-tier defense and infrastructure India has operationalized along the watershed.

3. Operational Command and Synergy: The frontlines are anchored by the Indian Army holds primary operational command and dominates key tactical heights, integrating paramilitary forces like ITBP seamlessly.

4. The Strategic Dilemma: Why hasn't the border been resolved? Both nations face insurmountable domestic political costs regarding territorial trade-offs. Furthermore, at the macro-strategic level, Beijing is acutely aware that a kinetic conflict with India offers zero strategic dividends—it risks disrupting critical sea lines of communication across the Indian Ocean and disproportionately benefits other global powers.

"At the macro-strategic level, a full-scale kinetic conflict offers no strategic victory for Beijing. The terrain friction of Himalayas serve as India’s defensive asset, and any major misadventure by China risks its maritime lifelines across Indian Ocean while serving third-party geopolitical interests." Shashi Asthana

results.title: India does need to strengthen its manufacturing base.
results.description:
India does need to strengthen its manufacturing base. That part of your argument is valid. But attributing the trade imbalance almost entirely to India's structural weaknesses is an incomplete analysis.

In FY26, India exported $19.47 billion to China while importing $131.63 billion. This is not just a manufacturing issue. It is also a question of reciprocal market access.

If Chinese companies enjoy access to India's vast market, Indian businesses should have comparable opportunities in China. Indian exporters continue to face regulatory and non tariff barriers.

India also has legitimate reasons to reduce excessive dependence on a country with which it has unresolved strategic and border tensions. Supply chain diversification is risk management, not necessarily protectionism.

India must become more competitive, but China must also make its market more accessible. Trade cannot be judged only by how efficiently one country sells. Reciprocity, transparency and mutual trust matter too.

A balanced trade relationship requires responsibility from both sides, not a lecture directed at India alone.

results.title: Look at how Instagram influencers spread propaganda.
results.description:
Look at how Instagram influencers spread propaganda.

A recent video by this influencer, Archana Pandit, about the alleged Chinese occupation of Arunachal Pradesh has already garnered 1.5 million views. Now, she is producing more videos on the same topic, apparently capitalising on the engagement.

However, the footage used in her videos has absolutely nothing to do with Arunachal Pradesh.

First clip: The footage presented as Chinese personnel assaulting residents of Arunachal Pradesh is actually from Hamid Karzai International Airport in Afghanistan, in 2021. It shows the chaos surrounding the withdrawal of US forces and the evacuation of civilians following the Taliban takeover of Afghanistan.

Second clip: The footage presented as residents of Arunachal Pradesh fleeing their homes is actually from Peru, a country in South America.

Third clip: The footage portrayed as a protest by people of Arunachal Pradesh against China actually shows Tibetans protesting against the Chinese occupation of Tibet.

Fourth clip: The footage shows an unrelated military movement, with no established connection to Arunachal Pradesh or the claims being made in the video.

This is how misleading narratives are manufactured. Meanwhile, the government's response remains largely limited to banning posts and blocking accounts in India. Even these restrictions are often temporary, with most accounts being unblocked in India within a few days. There seems to be little lasting accountability for those who repeatedly spread misinformation and manipulate public sentiment.

results.title: 20 jawans martyred in Galwan.
results.description:
20 jawans martyred in Galwan. And what did we get? “Na koi ghusa hai, na koi ghusa hua hai.” 🙂
Six years later:
– Arunachal: ITBP’s own DG says confrontations with Chinese troops are “continuing at multiple locations.” PLA tents reportedly pitched 6–7 km inside India’s side of the LAC.
– Assam: China is building the world’s largest dam on the Brahmaputra, Assam’s lifeline, right next to our border. Our response? “Monitoring.”
– Meanwhile, Xi Jinping was hosted in India last month like an old friend, handshakes and photo-ops.
56 inch ka seena only for opposition leaders, students and comedians. For China, it’s “dialogue,” “normalisation” and silence.
Mark my words: the man who sold himself as Mr Strongman will be remembered as the PM who blinked at Beijing. Desh ki suraksha pe compromise, aur voter bhoolta nahi. 🇮🇳🔥

results.title: India really didn’t have a problem with China in recent times, until Chinese soldiers decided to come for a picnic in the midst of a pandemi
results.description:
India really didn’t have a problem with China in recent times, until Chinese soldiers decided to come for a picnic in the midst of a pandemic to the Galwan valley in 2020. 

It’s laughable when a Chinese talks about fence setting and balancing. That’s exactly what you were doing between the Soviet Union and USA. So you can keep your gospel to yourself.

United States has critical technology and capital which India can benefit from, just the way China did. So we will continue to engage with USA even though they are difficult to deal with irrespective of what China thinks.

The government of India is elected by the people of the country. Good or bad is for them to decide, they are wise and will make changes whenever required. We are free people and not stymied by a dictator.

India isn’t some small island nation around China that it will kneel before another nation. It’s a civilisational state, it has its own knowledge, wisdom and thinking and will always act in its own interests. 

India will rise due to its own merits. China cannot curtail India’s growth, sure it can place obstacles and create bottlenecks at the most. When India flips China on incremental GDP growth in 2031, the world will be talking a different story. Enjoy the sunshine till then.
